A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 75 complete pages, including Appendices A–I. Text comparison and full-page rendering support reliable matching of the equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original numerical transferability demonstrations and trained-model size-generalization experiments on sets, graphs, and ModelNet10 point clouds, including appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original numerical demonstrations and size-generalization experiments in Section 6 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The DeepSet and DS-CI variants, GGNN, continuous GGNN, and SVD-DS retain the same architectures and computations. The revised formal assumptions do not change their procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same population-statistics, maximum-distance-from-origin, weighted-triangle-density, and ModelNet10 chair/sofa distance tasks, including the same appendix sampling scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments: the same DeepSet/PointNet, GNN/normalized 2-IGN/GGNN, and SVD-DS/DS-CI variants are evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix H retain identical splits, metrics, model budgets, training settings, and testing procedures, including graph sizes from 50 to 2000 and point-cloud sizes from 20 to 500.

E4.justification: The convergence demonstrations in Figures 2, 4, and 6 and prediction-versus-target diagnostics in Figures 7–10 are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary empirical analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both retain the 100-sample standard-deviation reporting, 10-run ranges or percentiles, and Figure 10's best-of-five initialization convention. No statistical reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: All experimental plots, error bars, predictions, and accompanying findings are unchanged, including appendix results. The revised analytical convergence bounds are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1 and Appendix C.1 now explicitly require equivariant maps. Corollaries E.6 and F.4 add sampling regularity assumptions; under newly stated integrability conditions, E.6 replaces logarithmic random-signal bounds with dimension-dependent polynomial bounds. E.6/G.3 replace generic p-dependent sampling formulas with Wasserstein-1 rates, while G.6 specifies Wasserstein-2 rates and a fourth-moment assumption. G.3/G.6 also replace d with the point-cloud dimension k. These materially revise quantitative guarantees and their hypotheses, although the underlying framework and proofs remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and stated contributions retain the same claims connecting transferability with continuity, deriving size-generalization guarantees, analyzing existing models, and designing transferable architectures.

C2.justification: The sampling guarantees receive more explicit applicability boundaries: Lipschitz grid signals/graphons and moment or boundedness conditions for random sampling. The broader interpretations of model-task alignment and Appendix I's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The code-access disclosure and Appendix H implementation details remain identical, including PyTorch, the NVIDIA A5000 GPU, optimizer settings, and training-time information.

R1.justification: The bibliography, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to prior transferability, representation-stability, and invariant-network research are unchanged.

P1.justification: Small wording and punctuation edits include adding 'the' to the introductory research question and correcting a quotation mark. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; section organization remains intact.

P2.justification: All figures and tables are visually unchanged. Revised equations and assumptions cause localized text reflow, including moving the concluding PointNet paragraph from page 45 to page 46.

improvement.justification: Explicit equivariance and sampling regularity requirements resolve omissions in v2 and improve theoretical precision. The gain is limited: G.6 still assumes only a fourth moment, whereas the invoked Appendix C.3 estimate requires q>4 for p=2. The main framework and empirical support remain unchanged.
